## What is *Delftia acidovorans*? {#about-delftia}

::: {.research-spotlight}
::: {.research-spotlight-text}
*Delftia acidovorans* is a gram-negative, non-fermentative bacterium first identified in Delft, Netherlands, in soil enriched with acetamide. It thrives in habitats containing high concentrations of heavy metals — copper, cobalt, and even **gold** — and produces a nonribosomal peptide that allows it to precipitate gold out of solution, avoiding toxicity.

Today, *Delftia* is found in waste-contaminated soil, water systems, and drains. Beyond its remarkable environmental capabilities, it is studied as an opportunistic pathogen and explored for applications in:

<span class="tag-chip">🏅 Gold Biomineralization</span>
<span class="tag-chip">♻️ E-Waste Recycling</span>
<span class="tag-chip">🌿 Bioremediation</span>
<span class="tag-chip">🧬 Genomics</span>
<span class="tag-chip">🔬 Undergraduate Research</span>

<br/><br/>
<a href="references.html" class="btn-hero btn-primary-hero" style="font-size:0.9rem;padding:0.55rem 1.4rem;">Read the Literature →</a>
:::
